chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Muhammad bin Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiya bin Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, what is the limit of a neighbor? He said: Forty houses from every side.

key_terms.جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a common honorific address to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the defined limit or boundary of a neighbor in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* establishes a precise geographical metric for neighborly rights, defining the scope as forty houses in each cardinal direction. This definition is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the applicability of specific social obligations, such as visiting, gift-giving, and conflict resolution, ensuring community cohesion extends beyond immediate proximity.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Mu’awiya bin Ammar, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, what is the limit of a neighbor? He said: Forty houses from every side.
